reasoning: Analogical synthesis: No structurally similar resolved cases exist in the vault's case library — this is the first documented shipborne hantavirus outbreak. The best analogs are Epuyen 2018-19 (Andes virus, 30+ cases in remote community, H2H burned out) and El Bolson 1996 (Andes, 16 cases, first documented H2H) — both involved the same pathogen with limited H2H, but in close-knit communities vs. globally dispersed cruise passengers, meaning the MV Hondius has lower contact density. The transport-vector-outbreak framework (two-phase pattern) predicts near-zero Phase 2 for inefficient H2H pathogens when aggressive contact tracing is active. Zero off-ship cases at cutoff despite active multinational surveillance, combined with WHO's 'no sign of larger outbreak' risk assessment, strongly limits the secondary spread. Starting from outside-view base rate of 36% (appointment/health reference class, structurally poor fit), adjusted downward for: reference class mismatch (-10%), inefficient Andes H2H reducing secondary attack rate (-8%), zero Phase 2 cases detected by cutoff despite active surveillance (-5%), small index denominator of 7 cases among 147 passengers (-3%), WHO risk assessment clearing immediate horizon (-2%). Partially offset by: Andes H2H capability (+3%), extended incubation window (up to 6 weeks, extending detection window to early June) (+2%), low 5-case threshold (+2%), multinational detection coordination challenges (+1%). Net adjustment -20% from base rate. Converges with Metaculus Cup crowd estimate of 0.20 for this question.

analogs.question: Andes virus outbreak in Epuyen, Argentina (2018-2019) — 30+ cases with documented H2H transmission
analogs.key_difference: Close-knit remote community vs. globally dispersed cruise passengers — contact density is much higher in Epuyen (household clusters, shared healthcare settings) vs. MV Hondius (passengers returned to 10+ countries with variable contact density)

analogs.question: First documented Andes virus H2H outbreak in El Bolson, Argentina (1996) — 16 cases
analogs.key_difference: Pre-internet detection environment with different surveillance capacity; first-ever documented H2H meant no contact tracing protocols existed; occurred in a small town where social networks are dense

analogs.question: Sin Nombre hantavirus outbreak in Yosemite National Park (2012) — 9 cases, tourist exposure in tent cabins
analogs.key_difference: Sin Nombre virus has NO H2H transmission, making it structurally different from the Andes virus involved in MV Hondius. Comparable on the transport-vector dimension (tourists dispersed post-exposure), but fundamentally different pathogen biology

analogs.question: SARS-CoV-2 outbreak on Diamond Princess cruise ship (2020) — ~700+ cases onboard
analogs.key_difference: SARS-CoV-2 is an efficiently H2H-transmissible respiratory virus with high R0 vs. Andes hantavirus which requires close/prolonged contact and has low secondary attack rate. Diamond Princess cases were primarily onboard (same enclosed environment), not off-ship secondary spread

flagged_surface_analogies.analogy: Diamond Princess / Grand Princess — 'cruise ship outbreaks always spread widely'
flagged_surface_analogies.why_misleading: SARS-CoV-2 is vastly more transmissible (high R0, airborne, asymptomatic transmission) than Andes hantavirus (requires close/prolonged contact, inefficient H2H, no asymptomatic transmission documented). Applying Diamond Princess dynamics to an Andes virus outbreak inflates P(secondary spread) by ignoring the pathogen characteristic that drives the outcome. The transport-vector framework correctly identifies pathogen H2H capability as the single most important variable.

flagged_surface_analogies.analogy: Norovirus cruise ship outbreaks — 'cruise ship outbreaks have high attack rates'
flagged_surface_analogies.why_misleading: Norovirus is shed in high concentrations in vomit/stool, transmitted via fomites and aerosols, with extremely low infectious dose (~18 virions). Hantavirus requires aerosolized rodent excreta or close/prolonged human contact (Andes only). The transmission mechanisms are entirely different, and the cruise ship enclosed environment amplifies norovirus far more than hantavirus.

flagged_surface_analogies.analogy: H5N1 agricultural spillover plateau — 'all zoonotic outbreaks plateau'
flagged_surface_analogies.why_misleading: While the plateau model (from zoonotic-outbreak-case-count-forecasting) is useful for non-H2H pathogens, Andes virus DOES have H2H capability, making it structurally different from H5N1 or Sin Nombre hantavirus. The plateau model applies only until H2H is confirmed — at which point partial escalation is possible. However, the historical Andes pattern (Epuyen at 30+, El Bolson at 16) shows even H2H Andes outbreaks plateau well below 100 cases.

adjustments.rationale: Outside-view base rate of 36% is from 'appointment/health' reference class containing structurally different question types (appointments, GDP releases, ceasefires, rate decisions). Outbreak secondary transmission questions have a structurally lower base rate.

Andes H2H requires close/prolonged household contact with low secondary attack rate (~10-20% among close contacts). Historical outbreaks (Epuyen 30+, El Bolson 16) burned out without sustained chains. With only 7 index cases among globally dispersed passengers, expected secondary cases = 7 * 3 contacts * 0.15 attack rate ~ 3.

Despite active international contact tracing under IHR mechanisms and 3+ weeks since first index case onset (April 6), zero off-ship cases had been publicly reported by May 21. This is informative even accounting for incubation lag — some household contacts should have been symptomatic by mid-May.

Only 7 confirmed/suspected cases among 147 passengers/crew. This limits the potential pool of close contacts who could become secondary cases. Small index cluster = small potential secondary case pool.

WHO's formal 'no sign of larger outbreak' assessment is the authoritative PIT signal that international surveillance found no evidence of sustained secondary transmission. While detection lags exist, this is a meaningful leading indicator that suppression efforts are working.

Unlike >99% of hantavirus strains, Andes CAN transmit human-to-human. The resolution threshold is only 5 linked off-ship cases, so even limited H2H could reach this bar if a single household cluster occurs.

Hantavirus incubation up to 6 weeks means secondary cases from the latest exposures (late April voyage end) may not be symptomatic until early June, after the cutoff. The August 1 deadline provides 10+ weeks for these to be detected and linked.

5 cases is a low bar. A single household cluster among one passenger's family (2-3 household contacts + 1-2 healthcare workers) could reach this threshold. The 'linked by a public health authority' criterion is broad and does not require proven H2H.

Passengers from 10+ countries with variable surveillance capacity and public health infrastructure. Detection lags in countries with weaker systems could delay case reporting, and some cases may be detected post-cutoff that were infected pre-cutoff.

what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence of a household cluster of Andes hantavirus among contacts of a single MV Hondius passenger would substantially increase P(5+ off-ship cases), as it would confirm H2H transmission efficiency in the current outbreak and provide a case-count multiplier. Conversely, reaching July 15, 2026 with zero or one reported off-ship cases would reduce the probability below 0.05, as the 6-week incubation window from the voyage would have closed and any remaining cases would require a transmission chain that would have been detected.
